questions.title: Assembly language trace
questions.text:
Assembly language mnemonics

| Mnemonic | Description |
|---|---|
| INP | Retrieve user input and stores it in the accumulator. |
| OUT | Output the value stored in the accumulator. |
| LDA | Load the Accumulator with the contents of the memory address given. |
| STA | Store the value in the Accumulator in the memory address given. |
| ADD | Add the contents of the memory address to the Accumulator. |
| SUB | Subtract the contents of the memory address from the Accumulator. |
| BRP | Branch/Jump to the address given if the Accumulator is zero or positive. |
| BRZ | Jump to the address given in case the Accumulator is zero. |
| BRA | Jump to the address given. |
| HLT | Stop the code. |
| DAT | Used to associate a label to a free memory address. An optional value can also be used to be stored at the memory address. |

An assembly language code is given below.

| Line number | Address | Instruction |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 00 | LABEL1    LDA COUNT |
| 2 | 01 | BRZ LABEL2 |
| 3 | 02 | SUB THREE |
| 4 | 03 | STA COUNT |
| 5 | 04 | LDA TOTAL |
| 6 | 05 | ADD EIGHT |
| 7 | 06 | STA TOTAL |
| 8 | 07 | OUT |
| 9 | 08 | BRA LABEL1 |
| 10 | 09 | LABEL2    HLT |
| 11 | 10 | EIGHT    DAT 008 |
| 12 | 11 | COUNT    DAT 006 |
| 13 | 12 | THREE    DAT 003 |
| 14 | 13 | TOTAL    DAT 000 |

parts.title: Seasons and testing (a)
parts.text:
Write a pseudocode or programming code to output the season name (spring, summer, autumn, or winter) according to the number of month entered by a user.

The code must show an error message if the entered number is incorrect.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Input number of month (1)
Use IF-ELSE statement. (1)
Use nested condition. (1)
Use OR operation. (1)
Output message for correct month number (1)
Output message for incorrect month number (1)
[Max 5]

Allow correct use of CASE statement for 2 marks to replace the 2 marks available for IF/Nested IF

points.criterion: Output message for correct month number
Output message for incorrect month number

scheme.model_answer:
INPUT month_number
IF month_number=1 OR month_number=2 OR month_number=12
   PRINT "Winter"
ELSE
   IF month_number=3 OR month_number=4 OR month_number=5
      PRINT "Spring"
   ELSE
      IF month_number=6 OR month_number=7 OR month_number=8
         PRINT "Summer"
      ELSE
         IF month_number=9 OR month_number=10 OR month_number=11
            PRINT "Autumn"
         ELSE
            PRINT "This month number is not exist"
scheme.ai_instructions: Award a maximum of 5 marks. Allow correct use of CASE statement for 2 marks to replace the 2 marks available for IF/Nested IF.

parts.title: Arrays and queue behaviour (b)
parts.text:
Scenario. A company assigns each worker with N tasks they have to complete by the end of the day. The activities list of a worker is stored in array ACTIVITIES.
The worker can take a Break only after completing the tasks stored in the array.

 e.g. ACTIVITIES [activity 1, activity 2, …, activity N, Break]).

The company wants to change the policy, so the day starts with a Break, after which the worker starts working on their activities.

 e.g. ACTIVITIES [Break, activity 1, activity 2, …, activity N]).

Write a pseudocode or programming code to change the order of activities and the break given in the array in accordance with the new policy of the company.

scheme.mark_scheme:
buf ← ACTIVITIES[N] (1)
For (1)
i from n downto 2 step – 1 (1)
  ACTIVITIES[i] := ACTIVITIES[i - 1]; (1)
endFor
ACTIVITIES[1] := buf (1)

points.criterion: Loop iterates i from n downto 2 step – 1
Moves each activity one position to the right: ACTIVITIES[i] := ACTIVITIES[i - 1]
Places saved break at the start: ACTIVITIES[1] := buf

scheme.model_answer:
buf ← ACTIVITIES[N]
For i from n downto 2 step – 1
  ACTIVITIES[i] := ACTIVITIES[i - 1]
endFor
ACTIVITIES[1] := buf

parts.title: Code analysis and optimisation (a)
parts.text:
Analyse the pseudocode below.

```pseudocode
N ← 100
K ← 0
FOR i FROM 0 TO N
   IF i MOD 2 = 0
   K = K + 1
ENDIF
ENDFOR
PRINT K
```

Explain the purpose of the given pseudocode.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Checks if a number is even in the range from 0 to 100 (1)
Prints the number of even numbers in a range (1)

points.criterion: Checks if a number is even in the range from 0 to 100
Prints the number of even numbers in a range

scheme.model_answer: The pseudocode checks each number from 0 to 100 to see whether it is even, counts the even numbers, and prints the number of even numbers in the range.
